tasks.title: Persist durable closure with retained evidence
tasks.goal: Record an explicit disposition whose evidence survives disposable cache loss.
steps: Define accepted/abandoned/superseded closure with exact intent/world/policy, authority and unresolved dispositions.
Retain evidence values or independently verifiable immutable references outside disposable lifecycle caches.
Apply closure through saved-state preconditions; exclude closure bytes from its own intent subject.
positive_cases: An explicit accepted closure retains enough evidence to inspect after cache deletion.
negative_cases: Cache-only IDs, truncated fact universe or stale subject cannot close.
Writing closure cannot mutate its own subject hash.
acceptance: Retained closure resolves each required proof independently of run cache.
Closure write is an explicit action with exact authored changes.
tasks.safe_stop: Prepared closure is inspectable before committed disposition.
notes: Internal children execute sequentially; cross-parent prerequisites remain exactly the root campaign graph.

tasks.title: Recompute closure applicability without erasing history
tasks.goal: Distinguish past acceptance from present readiness after drift.
steps: Revalidate retained intent/source/world/policy/output witnesses on closure inspection.
Mark applicability stale or proof unavailable while preserving historical disposition.
Exercise source updates, policy changes, output tamper and erased disposable caches.
positive_cases: Unchanged retained proof preserves applicability after cache cleanup.
negative_cases: Changed source/definition/policy/output cannot retain a fresh acceptance claim.
Missing retained immutable source is unavailable, not silently refreshed.
acceptance: Report separates historical decision, current applicability and missing proof.
No revalidation query mutates closure or reinstalls sources.
